memory_update.text: FORM should remain a priority underfollowed HBM sub-supplier because it has direct Q1 2026 evidence of record DRAM revenue driven by HBM applications and product-level evidence for HBM stack/interposer testing.

CAMT is one of the strongest direct-evidence names in the node after June 2026 orders from a tier-1 OSAT and leading HBM manufacturer, plus Hawk platform positioning for HBM, chiplets, hybrid bonding, and micro-bump inspection.

For HBM and advanced packaging, the best underfollowed US-listed sub-supplier lanes appear to be probe cards, inspection/metrology, and bonding equipment; generic semiconductor equipment screens may miss these narrower exposures.

COHU remains a possible shadow candidate in sockets/contactors/handlers and semiconductor test interfaces, but this pass did not find HBM-specific evidence strong enough to include it over FORM, CAMT, KLIC, and AMKR.

node: HBM and advanced-packaging sub-suppliers below memory producers
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a compact US-listed universe where the underfollowed lane is strongest in probe cards, inspection/metrology, and thermocompression bonding rather than generic semiconductor equipment. The most direct evidence points to FormFactor for HBM/DRAM probe cards and Camtek for HBM and advanced-packaging inspection/metrology orders. Kulicke & Soffa is a narrower thermocompression-bonding hypothesis tied to AI advanced packaging, but needs verification of HBM-specific mix. Amkor is included as a reference/context anchor because it is a US-listed OSAT with advanced packaging and test capacity, but it is less obscure and more of a capacity owner than a sub-supplier.
